entry_point.discipline_context: Use potential energy, equilibrium, and numerical relaxation to motivate an optimisation landscape.
entry_point.rationale: Second-year mechanical engineers can connect a downhill search direction with reducing a scalar energy-like objective before formalising the mathematics.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The energy picture is a teaching analogy: the canonical formulation is an arbitrary differentiable objective, so no physical interpretation is assumed unless stated.

chapter_sequence.title: From equilibrium to an optimisation problem
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce the unconstrained mathematical problem and first- and second-order optimality conditions through a careful potential-energy analogy.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and conditioning
chapter_sequence.purpose: Define the geometric assumptions that control local models, global lower bounds, and numerical difficulty.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and choosing a step
chapter_sequence.purpose: State the gradient descent update, common fixed-step choices, exact line search, and Armijo backtracking.

chapter_sequence.title: What convergence guarantees actually say
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present convex and strongly convex convergence statements with their hypotheses, then compare momentum and acceleration.

chapter_sequence.title: Stochastic and adaptive gradient methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain empirical objectives, stochastic-gradient assumptions, diminishing steps, and the semantics of AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam.

chapter_sequence.title: Second-order optimisation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce Newton and BFGS as curvature-aware methods, including implementation cautions and local convergence scope.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Consolidate assumptions, one update calculation, and a Python diagnosis in a final exercise chapter.

implementation_strategy: Use compact NumPy-style pseudocode and one executable Python block. Emphasise evaluating the gradient at the specified iterate, preserving indices, solving Newton systems, and checking objective decrease rather than assuming it.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly three final exercises: an assumption-scope concept check reviewed by an expert, a deterministic hand calculation with an objective-gradient consistency check, and an executable code diagnostic.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Distinguish stationarity, second-order conditions, and theorem scope in an equilibrium-style optimisation statement.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Assess a claimed equilibrium of a reduced potential-energy model for a linkage.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Apply the standard gradient descent update and verify a supplied quadratic objective and gradient.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Take one relaxation step for a two-parameter quadratic calibration objective.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Diagnose whether Python implements the current-iterate gradient descent rule and identify the effect of a sign error.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Inspect a short NumPy relaxation loop for a quadratic stiffness-fitting objective.
